niche_preference_profile: This user prefers clean, modern, app-like interfaces that feel spacious but still information-rich. They like strong visual hierarchy, clear sectioning, readable typography, and obvious primary actions. They tend to prefer layouts that are well-populated and functional rather than sparse or placeholder-like, but they dislike clutter, excessive chrome, and overly verbose copy. They also show a strong preference for polished, finished-looking screens with clear controls, visible state, and easy scanning.

criteria.description: Clear headline-first structure with distinct separation between title, supporting content, and settings/actions.
Fewer, clearly separated sections or cards with coherent grouping of related controls.
Bold, crisp, easy-to-scan headings and labels with strong contrast and legibility.
Short, direct explanatory text that gets to the point quickly without long paragraphs.
A refined, finished, app-like visual style rather than a plain, system-form, or draft-like look.
A visually obvious main CTA or next-step button that stands out clearly from secondary actions.
Related controls, especially settings and permissions, should be grouped into tidy, easy-to-scan clusters.
Moderately dense screens that feel populated and complete, but not crowded or overloaded.
Interfaces should feel fully populated and intentional, not sparse, partial, or placeholder-like.
Toggles, rows, and settings should be presented in a straightforward, low-friction way with minimal visual noise.
Copy and visual tone should feel calm, friendly, and reassuring rather than sterile, harsh, or alarmist.
Minimal top chrome, restrained progress indicators, and low-distraction navigation framing.
Settings and list items should have obvious labels, visible states, and easy-to-distinguish on/off or active/inactive cues.
Rows and modules should be easy to scan vertically, with consistent separators and clear affordances.
Subtle, balanced accent colors are preferred over overly dominant or harsh color treatment.
